ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Mary Seacole Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Visit for headaches on waking and knee pain with a fall: very high blood pressure found, without target-organ emergency; examination, ECG, laboratory tests, home monitoring, knee osteoarthritis, falls screen, her own remedies, and geriatric medicine referral. Concerns: She wants to keep walking to see her friends without fear of falling; She wants her own knowledge as a healer, and her remedies, respected rather than dismissed; She worries about the cost of medicines and getting to appointments. [S]

tr.td: Diclofenac sodium 1% topical gel, 4 g rubbed into each painful knee up to four times a day
4 g to each knee up to four times a day
Amlodipine 5 mg oral tablet, one tablet daily
Chlorthalidone 12.5 mg oral tablet, one tablet each morning
Atorvastatin 20 mg oral tablet, one tablet daily
Losartan 25 mg oral tablet, one tablet daily
Twelve-lead electrocardiogram: sinus rhythm at 76 per minute; left ventricular hypertrophy by voltage criteria with no strain pattern; no ischemia or arrhythmia
Transthoracic echocardiography: ejection fraction 64%; mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy; normal valves; grade 1 diastolic dysfunction; no heart failure
Advance care planning conversation, about 25 minutes, with her consent
Tetanus, diphtheria, and acellular pertussis vaccine (Tdap)

list.item: Nurse, healer and writer; asked to be called Mrs. Seacole; known to many former soldiers and their families; still gives nursing advice to neighbours who call on her [S]

Widowed for many years, with no children; lives alone in rented rooms up two flights of stairs in Paddington; friends visit, but she goes out less since her fall and some weeks speaks to few people [S]
Income: a modest fixed income from savings and the fund raised for her; careful with money since her bankruptcy, and worried about the cost of medicines, a blood pressure cuff and taxis [S]

Her own remedies: ginger tea most days; a liquorice root infusion for coughs on and off; a liniment she makes with camphor and oil of wintergreen, which she massages into her knees; she shared these openly and wants them respected [S]
Diet: home cooking with rice, peas, fish, vegetables and fruit, and salted fish and pickled foods several times a week; tea with sugar; never smoked; a small glass of wine on occasions [S]
Strengths, supports and purpose: decades of nursing and healing, courage, humour, her writing and her friendships with old soldiers; she wants to keep walking to see her friends [S]

tr.td: Visit for headaches on waking and knee pain with a fall: very high blood pressure found, without target-organ emergency; examination, ECG, laboratory tests, home monitoring, knee osteoarthritis, falls screen, her own remedies, and geriatric medicine referral
One-week review with geriatric medicine: home readings confirm stage 2 hypertension; two first-line medicines; comprehensive geriatric assessment of falls, function, mood and social needs
Four-week review: blood pressure, sodium and potassium on chlorthalidone, echocardiogram, statin decision, knee exercise program and cane
Three-month review after chlorthalidone was stopped: blood pressure above target, losartan added; lipids on atorvastatin; knee and falls
Six-month review: blood pressure at target, screening and bone density results, knee function, falls and social connection
Same-day sick visit for dizziness on standing during a cold

Dignified, culturally safe care: address her as Mrs. Seacole; respect her expertise as a nurse and healer; ask about her remedies openly and check them for interactions without dismissing them; explain each choice plainly and let her decide; solve access barriers (a free home blood pressure cuff in a large size, transport, the stairs) rather than treat them as non-adherence

Geriatric medicine consultation within one week for a comprehensive geriatric assessment: falls, blood pressure targets and medicine choices in an older woman living alone, knee osteoarthritis, mood and social needs

Confirm the blood pressure: home readings twice daily for seven days with a validated upper-arm monitor and a large cuff, technique taught; ECG, metabolic panel, lipids, hemoglobin A1c, TSH, urine albumin and blood count today; an echocardiogram for stage 2 readings with ECG voltage for left ventricular hypertrophy; treatment decided at the one-week review

Knee osteoarthritis: exercise therapy with a physical therapist, then a tai chi class at the community center; diclofenac 1% gel; a 5% weight loss; a cane, fitted and used in the right hand; no oral anti-inflammatory medicines because of her blood pressure and kidneys; a corticosteroid injection as an option for a flare

Falls (STEADI): screen, then Timed Up and Go, 30-second chair stand, 4-stage balance test and orthostatic blood pressure at visits; medicine review against the Beers criteria; vision and footwear checks; a home safety visit by an occupational therapist, with a rail for the stairs to her rooms; exercise for strength and balance

Her own remedies, checked with her: liquorice root can raise blood pressure and lower potassium, so she will pause it while her blood pressure is treated (her decision); ginger tea in food amounts is fine; her camphor and wintergreen liniment contains a salicylate, so it is used on a different knee or at a different time from the diclofenac gel, never under a heat pad, and kept away from the eyes

Loneliness and costs: a social prescribing link worker; the tai chi group and a lunch club near her home; a check of the help she is entitled to with costs and transport; generic medicines and a 90-day supply
Lifestyle: less salted fish and pickled food, more vegetables and fruit, regular walking, and alcohol kept to occasions

Two first-line medicines for stage 2 hypertension: amlodipine 5 mg and chlorthalidone 12.5 mg each morning, with sodium, potassium and creatinine in about four weeks and orthostatic readings at each visit; target below 130/80 mmHg; sick-day rule: stop chlorthalidone and call if she cannot eat or drink normally, or has vomiting or diarrhea
Atorvastatin 20 mg daily (moderate intensity) for a 10-year cardiovascular risk of about 14% with LDL 146 mg/dL; lipid panel in four to twelve weeks
Chlorthalidone stopped for hyponatremia and hypokalemia with orthostatic hypotension; eat normally with some salt for a few days; sodium recheck in one week
Losartan 25 mg daily added to amlodipine 5 mg, with potassium and creatinine in two to four weeks; blood tests drawn at home by the community nurse when a separate trip would be needed
Blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg at home and in the clinic, without dizziness on standing
128/76 in the clinic and 126/74 at home on amlodipine and losartan, with no orthostatic drop
No headaches since the second week of treatment
Knee pain 3 or less out of 10 and walking 20 minutes a day with a cane
Pain 3 out of 10; KOOS JR 52.5 to 66.2; walks 20 minutes most days
No falls in six months; one near-fall during the sodium problem, without injury

list.item: Independent in personal care; manages her own medicines and money; carries heavy shopping with difficulty and avoids the stairs when her knees are bad; walks with no aid [S]
Alert, warm and quick-witted; describes her symptoms with a nurse's precision; worried about falling and about cost; mood a little low when alone [S]
